name: Neo4j
model: Property graph: nodes and relationships with labels and key-value properties, queried with Cypher (and GQL)
engine_note: Native graph store: records point directly at neighbouring nodes and relationships, so traversals follow pointers instead of joins
consistency: ACID multi-statement transactions; READ COMMITTED isolation, so lost updates and non-repeatable reads are possible unless you take explicit write locks. Clustering (Enterprise) gives causal consistency via bookmarks; secondaries can be stale.
scaling: Bigger machine first; Enterprise clusters add read replicas (secondaries) and Raft primaries; multiple and composite databases or sharded property databases for very large graphs.

licence_events.event: Neo4j 3.5 (first release candidate tagged 2018-11-16): Enterprise Edition becomes closed source, commercial licence only (3.4 had been AGPLv3 plus Commons Clause); Community stays GPLv3

version_note: Calendar versioning since 2025.01; date is the tagged commit date on GitHub.
reach: Reach for it when queries walk many hops of relationships (fraud rings, recommendations, knowledge graphs, permissions) and SQL joins get deep.
avoid: Avoid when your data is mostly rows and aggregates, or you need clustering without Enterprise licences or AuraDB.
escape: multi-hop relationship queries that take many recursive joins in Postgres are one short Cypher pattern
chat: Knowledge graph of entities mentioned across chats, for retrieval that follows relationships (GraphRAG).
notes: Licence verified: GitHub repo licence GPL-3.0 (Community); operations manual says Community is 'Open source under GPLv3' and Enterprise is commercial; Enterprise-only: clustering, online backup, RBAC, multiple databases, composite and sharded property databases. Isolation quoted from the concurrent data access page: read committed, with lost updates, non-repeatable reads, missing and double reads possible. 'Causal consistency via bookmarks' is from the clustering docs and was not re-fetched today. The 2018 licence-change date is the 3.5.0-rc01 tag date; the open-core page (dated 2026-09-11 as fetched) gives the change by version, not day. No Jepsen analysis of Neo4j exists.
